time on his record mr lee riston has proved himself to be the kind of citizen that robbins has been looking for mr riston came to robbins about years ago from chicago where he received his grammar school education and graduated from the du sable high school while in du cable attained the rank of commanding officer for years from the he later joinned the illinois national guard became st lieutenant in the militia after coming to robbins mr riston wasted no time in becoming affiliated with the civic affairs of the village he was a member of robbins fire department in he was elected to the office of village trustee being new to the position of chairman of streets to which he was appointed after his election it took some time for him to find his way but in a very short time he had grasped the situation and had things well in hand mr riston gave the village of robbins a very remarkable improvement on the streets it was mr riston who first introduced the idea of placing a booster pump on the water lines it was a bitter fight but he won today if the pump is not running the village is completely without water mr riston lives with his wife and two children at th and hamlin avenue robbins illinois he is also quite a sportsman being president of the robbins gun and rod club of robbins he is employed years with the perfection gear of harvey illinois as supervisor at a very good salary one can see at a glance that mr riston is a wide mr lee riston awake young man and is quite active in village and civic affairs as chairman of the health committee mr riston has done much to help rid the village of some of its health menaces this has caused him to issue warrants to some citizens to appear in court before they would act bei ing trained in the army an ofder is to be carried out he knows nothing but to see that laws are carried out i don't know if mr riston is going to try to succeed himself as trustee of the village but if he should then i am sure the citizens of robbins will never forget the good job mr riston has done what is mrs white's game do you know the political pot is boiling in the village of robbins the non partisan party the first to hold a mass meeting in the fight to elect three village trustees chose mrs elinor white as the keynote speaker there was given the greatest display of hypocrisy and ignorance that one ever witnessed it is a pity that the people can be so misinformed in one voice the people neard that the village clerk had a perfect record and heard the same person say that they didn't know what was going on in the village hall it is a sad affair that this village has a clerk who would attempt to use a liquor ordinance which was passed in when the state had a law on selling beverages with alcohol one doesn't have to be a drinker to know that there must be another ordinance passed at a later date to take care of beverages with a much higher alcoholic content yet our village clerk is hopelessly trying to criticize the mayor inasmuch as all monies are turned over to the village clerk why is it so important that she must collect the liquor license monies for two years mrs white never worried about collecting anything but the checks which were made out to one mrs hyde or mrs robinson can she be looking for something to fill the gap left after she could no longer get these checks at long last a real step has been taken to modernize our village robbins village board met thursday evening at the village hall for the purpose of studying the resolution from the reconstruction fin ance corporation on the loan of to improve the water supply and to put in sewers this resolution is a contract between the village oi robbins and the reconstruction finance corporation after the village clerk had read and the engineers explained each paragraph of the contract the trustees then passed the resolution in its entirety this is the first step the second step will be to pass the bond issue in the amount of the two engineers are walter wilson engineer for the project and george jones engineer for the village of robbins notice the original citizens forty has filed its ticket with the village clerk marcellus jones lee riston and victor anderson are the candidates on this ticket vote for a continuation of the sewer and water project and better housing mrs elinor white was elected on the original citizens party ticket two years ago after she had left the non partisan party because she said the non partisan party was so rotten they were nothing but hoodlums but today she wants those same hoodlums to come to the village hall and help her now what does she want them to help her do i don't think the people of robbins want those kind of people in the village hall including mrs white

for your consideration mr victor anderson a young man who has a very colorful record he attended the grade schools here in robbins attended and graduated from tilden tech high school chicago illinois mr anderson is a very quiet and unassuming young man but a deep thinker ana stanas last as the hoc of gibraltar he is a member of robbins fire departmentassistant chief chairman of i union at libby mcneil libby for years worked there as a supervisor for years and is now a processor for the same company he has been employed at libby's for years he also won the south suburban boxing championship mr anderson has served two terms as village trustee of the village of robbins he lives with his wife and three children in their home at trumble avenue mr anderson was elected to office in on the nonpartsan party ticket he has been an asset to the office for some unknown reason the non partisan did not ask mr anderson nor marcellus jones to run on their ticket because of the good work of anderson riston and jones they have all been chosen to run on the original citizens party ticket mr anderson with his fellow trustees are a perfect team all are for the betterment of this village mr branch was continued until march th at the request of defendant wolford charles johnson of morgan park was served with a court order to repair damages done to an open letter to citizens of robbins in general and to armstrong directly why there is no water we are wondering if the reverend armstrong proposed to tell his readers why there is no water or if it was his intention to tell them to whom to report the situation or does he just wish to make some idle remarks for your information rev armstrong the water condition in the village of robbins is well known by the county health department the health department the cook county board and every other agency that you can name this being a fact the only advice the village board could get was the village needs a reservoir and a larger pipe line to supply its citizens it so happens that it takes money to put in these larger pipe lines to the amount of and even now some people are crabbing about paying per month for water an investigation of the records at the village hall will disclose the fact that a large percentage of the water users are not paying even the per month for water there is another percentage who has large houses and is renting them out and pay only per month when they should be paying per month for each family for your further information the village board has secured a loan to put this larger pipe line through it is true that the village is open to epidemics diseases not only because of the shortage of water but because some citizens have so much filth and garbage around their homes everybody can clean that up it should always be remembered people living in glass houses should never throw stones if our leaders especially the preachers would do more constructive teaching on how to live instead of criticizing there is lots of work to be done in this village and the preachers could play a most important part in helping to get it done the squad car the decision was lauded by some members of the oard the case of the people versus chester canada was sent on a change of venue to judge andrews at the state department accidents in the village of robbins have been numerous and the police department has gone all out to apprehend traffic violators and when caught and convicted to give i them the full penalty of the law

two years ago switched to the non partisans in this election today mayor john richardson stands alone with six trustees and the village clerk against him this as we all know is a very unfortunate position in which to be the non partisans control the village board they are in the saddle the eyes of the citizens of robbins are on this board they are watching to see if these men show any disposition to fulfill their promises of better lighting surface drainage more water and sewerage a big job for men who have no experience in such matters and are practically unknown outside the village and whose influence does not reach beyond the boundaries of robbins but the people have spoken and the job is theirs if a fair proportion of this job is to be accomplished then politics must of a model clean desirable place to live namely here perhaps it is too much to reason that robbins could become a picture book village over night but with a little constructive planning and civic interest the could change quickly as an example of what civic minded citizens can do is best shown by the progress made in then ew sub division of hometown lying just west and north of robbins this suburban development grew from a prairie four years ago to a town of over while it is not the intentiono this column to mislead you on the facts and try to compare the village with a fully developel improved community for whites i do propose to show how people working together can accomplish almost any desirable aim hometown has a modern police force of volunteer members headed by a single salaried chief the force is equipped with one police car with a two way radio this was a contribution of the people their new police station lacking a jail was also given by the public each member of order are maintained and they have gained the respect of most outsiders in contrast robbing police are poorly trained lack worth while equipment and seem to work in confusion at times they are not supported by the people as a whole and the funds for rectifying the situation are just not forthcoming with more careful planning and active interest on the part of the citizens we too could have a modern police force this particular comparison of our police with those of hometown's is not the only facet in a series of comparisons that could be made with communities even smaller than robbins the
